sections.h2: Who records deeds in Lawrence County
sections.html:
The Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds is a combined office serving the county seat of New Castle. The Recorder's main duty is recording, protecting, preserving and reproducing legal documents that relate to real estate.

The same office collects county recording fees, the Real Estate Transfer Tax owed to the state, local municipalities and school districts, and the fees that state law sends to the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts. For anyone selling a house in Lawrence County, one counter takes the tax and the fee and files the deed.

Ask the office for its current hours and its last time to accept a deed on a given day, since your title company's schedule depends on it.

Records reach back to the founding of the county in 1849, and all real estate records are open to the public. Older books are searched in the office, while more recent years can be searched online.

The online service runs on CountyFusion and lets you search, view and print documents dating to about 1970. The county also offers a quick land-records search from its cloud search page, and a free property alert service launched in October 2022 that warns an owner when a document is recorded against their property.

  • Use the online index to pull the previous deed and copy the legal description exactly.
  • Check that the name on the old deed matches the name of the person signing the new one.
  • Look for old mortgages that still show as open, and ask the lender for a satisfaction if one was paid off.

Lawrence County accepts e-recording, which the office describes as simple, fast and money-saving. It names four vendors on its website: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. Closing agents who already use one of these can send the deed in without a courier.

Paper still works. A deed can be carried in or mailed to the Recorder, but you need the exact total in the right form, so call the office for a figure before you write a check. The Recorder's page also carries notices about a state-mandated fee increase and a separate increase in the parcel ID fee, so don't rely on an old fee sheet.

A fee sheet from the county's Redevelopment Authority gives a concrete picture for a deed. It lists deed recording at $87.75 plus $20.00 for each parcel purchased.

Recording charges on a Lawrence County fee sheet
ChargeAmount
Deed recording$87.75
Added per parcel purchased$20.00
Realty transfer tax2% (1% state, 1% local)
Statement of Value, if tax exempt$2.00

Treat these numbers as a guide and get the real total from the Recorder, because the add-ons change with the page count and the number of parcels.

The county's Assessment Office assigns parcel IDs and provides a form to request a new one. A deed that covers more than one parcel costs more to record.

Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state tax on the value of the transfer, and the Department of Revenue holds both grantor and grantee liable. The county fee sheet shows the local share as another 1 percent, for a combined 2 percent.

The Recorder sends the state's part to Harrisburg and the rest to the municipality and school district. Certain family transfers, transfers to government, and property that passes by will or intestacy are exempt, but a Statement of Value is still filed to show why.

  • A sale to an outside buyer is an ordinary transfer, so an estate selling a house should plan for the tax in its settlement figures.
  • If title first passes to an heir, the Register of Wills side of the same office can say what paperwork it wants.

It values the county's roughly 56,000 parcels, which cover 367 square miles across 27 municipalities. One of them is the city of New Castle, with 8 wards, and the others are nine boroughs and sixteen townships. Ellwood City's second ward lies partly in Beaver County.

The office also runs the Act 72 Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion and the Clean and Green program, and it keeps the county's GIS tax maps. Its forms page lists a sales verification form, a change of address form, and a property owner contact form tied to Act 29 of 2026.

The Assessment Board meets monthly. If you sell a homestead property, ask the office how the sale affects the exclusion, and update your mailing address with its change of address form.

Lawrence County has 83,911 residents in the July 2025 estimate, down 2.5% since April 2020, and 39,704 housing units. Owners live in 75.8% of homes for 2020 to 2024, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $147,200. Median gross rent is $831.

sections.h2: Steps from signing to recorded deed
sections.html:
Start with the old deed. Pull it from the online index, copy the legal description exactly, and confirm the seller's name matches. Next, list each parcel by its ID from the Assessment Office. The deed is then signed and notarized at closing.

The closing agent adds a Statement of Value if tax is excused or the price isn't stated, and totals the recording fee, the $20.00 per parcel charge and the transfer tax. The package goes in electronically through one of the four vendors or on paper to the New Castle office. The Recorder files the deed, sends the tax to the state, municipality and school district, and the new owner enters the public record.

Afterward, check that any paid-off mortgage shows a satisfaction. An open mortgage on the record can slow the next buyer's title search, so ask your lender to file it.

sections.h2: What to bring to record a Lawrence County deed
sections.html:
Pull these together before the closing date.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the full legal description.
  • The parcel ID for each parcel being conveyed.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or the price is not stated.
  • Payment for the recording fee, the parcel ID charge and the transfer tax, in the form the office accepts.
  • A return address for the recorded deed.

If a title company is handling the sale, confirm that they file electronically through one of the four vendors and ask when the recorded copy will arrive. A cash buyer skips the lender's steps, but this list stays the same.

faqs.q: Does Lawrence County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder of Deeds lists four e-recording vendors on the county site: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. A closing agent with an account at one of them can submit the deed without a trip to New Castle.

faqs.q: How far back can I search Lawrence County deeds online?
faqs.a: The online system covers documents from about 1970 forward. County records start with the formation of the county in 1849, and the older volumes are searched in the office.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Lawrence County home sale?
faqs.a: The combined rate on the county fee sheet is 2 percent, made up of 1 percent state tax and 1 percent local tax. Exempt transfers, such as some family transfers, file a Statement of Value instead.

faqs.q: Is there a way to be warned if someone records a document on my property?
faqs.a: Yes. The county offers a free property alert service, launched in October 2022, as fraud protection. Ask the Recorder's office how to sign up.

faqs.q: What office issues parcel IDs in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: The county Assessment Office. It posts a Request for a New Parcel ID Number form, and it can tell you which parcels a deed must name. Every parcel on a deed adds to the recording cost.
